A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable main text, equations, proofs, tables and experimental appendices. Content can be matched across the substantial reformatting and figure renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 1.1 and 5 and Appendix G report original training experiments and synthetic convergence measurements, including comparisons between linear and convolutional models.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical results and adds experiments with larger initialization norms in Appendix G.4, Figures 29–30.

M1.justification: The models, gradient-descent reductions and perceptron update rules are retained. Section 5's added explanation of selecting the first sample when both are misclassified clarifies the existing two-sample algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic two-sample problem and CIFAR-10, EuroSAT, FashionMNIST, Food101, MNIST and Gisette coverage. The new initialization sweep changes model settings within an existing task.

E2.justification: The linear-versus-convolutional and classical-versus-quadratic perceptron comparisons retain their comparison methods. The new initialization experiments refer back to the existing linear-model baseline without introducing another comparator.

E3.justification: New Appendix G.4 evaluates the existing CIFAR-10 experiment with initial weights multiplied by 10 and 100. This adds a limited initialization-setting sweep; the previously reported experimental protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix G.4 adds a robustness analysis asking whether implicit acceleration persists with larger initialization norms, supported by accuracy, loss and iterate-norm trajectories. Existing dimensionality, kernel-size and norm-growth analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report 30 randomly initialized runs per candidate step size for Figure 2 and retain its shaded bands. V2 introduces no additional run-count, seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing reporting.

E6.justification: Figures 29–30 add results for 10-fold and 100-fold initialization scaling, showing that the nonlinear model still separates faster than the retained linear baseline. Earlier results remain, including the approximately 330K-versus-20K iteration comparison and Table 2's step sizes 0.0158, 0.0079 and 0.0020.

T1.justification: Theorem 5.2 explicitly extends the classical-perceptron lower bound to any positive step size phi, changing the initialization condition from B(0, epsilon) to B(0, phi epsilon). Appendix E adds the scaling-invariance argument; the bound and other substantive proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims about perceptron reductions, dimension-dependent implicit acceleration on a minimalistic example, multilayer extensions and empirical support.

C2.justification: The conclusion newly identifies extending the large-norm theory to the small-norm regime as future work. Appendix G.4 interprets the added experiments as robustness to initialization magnitude; existing MNIST qualifications and broader-model limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix G newly specifies disabled bias weights and the default PyTorch uniform initialization distributions for linear and convolutional layers. These are additional disclosures, without evidence that retained experiments changed; hardware and software descriptions remain.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and Section 7's research positioning are unchanged. Fuller bibliographic details, including the SymPy DOI and corrected author metadata, concern existing references.

P1.justification: V2 adds short explanations and a robustness subsection, revises the conclusion, updates affiliations, and adds acknowledgements and an impact statement. It removes the contents list, while retaining the main section sequence and most prose.

P2.justification: The main text changes to a two-column conference layout with running headers and reflowed equations. Plots throughout are resized and restyled, Figure 28 changes its norm axis from logarithmic to linear, two figures are added, and the retained ResNet figure moves from Figure 29 to Figure 31.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility through initialization and bias disclosures, adds focused initialization-robustness evidence, and makes the lower bound's step-size scope explicit. The small-norm limitation is also clearer. Removing the contents list slightly harms navigation, but these targeted scientific and documentation improvements provide a modest net benefit.
